items.stem: Spoke A is peered to a hub, and the hub is peered to spoke B. Spoke A cannot reach spoke B. Why?

options.text: VNet peering is non-transitive; spoke-to-spoke needs gateway/route transit or a hub NVA
options.rationale: Correct: peering is not transitive by default.

options.text: Peering always routes all traffic automatically
NSGs block all peered traffic by design
options.rationale: NSGs are explicit, not the cause here.

options.text: Spokes cannot be peered to a hub
options.rationale: They can; transitivity is the issue.

items.explanation: Correct: peering is not transitive by default.

items.stem: Which TWO factors favour ExpressRoute over a site-to-site VPN for a regulated workload? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Traffic stays off the public internet over a private circuit
options.rationale: Correct: ExpressRoute uses a private connection.

options.text: Higher, more predictable bandwidth and SLA
options.rationale: Correct: ExpressRoute offers consistent throughput and an SLA.

options.text: It is always cheaper than a VPN

options.rationale: It requires provider and edge configuration.

items.explanation: Correct: ExpressRoute uses a private connection.

items.stem: A security team requires all internet egress to be inspected by a firewall appliance. What steers VNet traffic to it?

options.text: A user-defined route sending 0.0.0.0/0 to the appliance's internal IP
options.rationale: Correct: a UDR overrides system routes to force egress through the NVA.

options.text: An NSG allow rule on the subnet
options.rationale: NSGs filter but do not redirect routing.
Peering connects networks; it does not force inspection.
DNS resolves names; it does not route egress.

items.explanation: Correct: a UDR overrides system routes to force egress through the NVA.
